data.name: Arjunan
data.long_meaning: Arjuna, the name of a legendary warrior in Hindu mythology. Derived from the Sanskrit word arjuna, meaning 'bright, bold, or shining.' Arjuna was the greatest warrior of the Mahabharata war, known for his bravery, devotion, and wisdom. He was guided by Lord Krishna, who imparted the Bhagavad Gita teachings, making Arjuna an embodiment of righteousness and the pursuit of duty over desire.

data.cultural_impact: The name Arjuna holds a significant place in Indian culture, being the name of a revered warrior and central character in one of the greatest epics, the Mahabharata. Arjuna's bravery and unwavering loyalty to his duty, as portrayed in the epic, have inspired countless generations and continue to leave a lasting impact on Indian society.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Arjuna holds immense spiritual significance as he was the chosen warrior and disciple of Lord Krishna. Krishna imparted the teachings of the Bhagavad Gita to Arjuna, emphasizing the importance of selfless action, detachment from material desires, and the pursuit of righteousness, leading Arjuna to be remembered not just as a warrior but as a spiritual icon.

He is a warrior in the Kuru kingdom and is widely regarded as one of the greatest warriors in ancient India. Arjuna is also a key figure in the Bhagavad Gita, a 700-verse Hindu scripture in Sanskrit of which approximately 77 chapters form a part of the sixth book of the Mahabharata. In this text, Arjuna learns the art of warfare from the god Krishna.

He is also the charioteer of the god Krishna, who acts as his mentor and guide in the war.
